questions.q: During the Delhi Sultanate period, which one of the following taxes was levied on treasure looted in war?
questions.solution:
Khums was levied on war booty. The term refers to a one-fifth share.

**Answer: Khums**

questions.q: Where did the Gaddi tribe’s shepherds live in the fourteenth century?
questions.solution:
Gaddi pastoral communities lived in the western Himalayas, including present-day Himachal Pradesh.

**Answer: Western Himalayas**

questions.q: As of 31st July 2025, which of the following country is NOT the member of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations?
questions.solution:
Pakistan is not an ASEAN member. Indonesia, Malaysia and the Philippines are members.

**Answer: Pakistan**

questions.q: Which of the following is the joint military exercise between India and Nepal?
questions.solution:
Surya Kiran is the bilateral military exercise between India and Nepal.

**Answer: Surya Kiran**

questions.q: What name was given to Bal Gangadhar Tilak by the British rulers?
options: The Father of the Indian Unrest
questions.solution:
Tilak was described as the father of Indian unrest in British commentary on the nationalist movement.

**Answer: The Father of the Indian Unrest**

questions.q: Who was the first recipient of the Best Actor at the National Film Awards?
questions.solution:
Uttam Kumar was the first recipient of the National Film Award for Best Actor, introduced in 1967.

**Answer: Uttam Kumar**

questions.q: "UDISE+" which was in news in February 2025, is related to which of the following sector?
questions.solution:
UDISE+ is the Unified District Information System for Education Plus. It collects school education data.

**Answer: Education**

questions.q: In Union Budget 2025-26, Jal Jeevan Mission has been extended until _______.
questions.solution:
The Union Budget 2025–26 announced extension of the Jal Jeevan Mission until 2028.

**Answer: 2028**

questions.q: Which of the following sports is played on water?
questions.solution:
Surfing involves riding waves on water. The other sports listed are played on land.

**Answer: Surfing**

questions.q: The term Decathlon and Heptathlon are related to which of the following?
questions.solution:
Decathlon and heptathlon combine multiple track-and-field disciplines. They are athletics events.

**Answer: Athletics events**

questions.q: Volleyball was introduced in the Asian Games in ____ for women.
questions.solution:
Women’s volleyball entered the Asian Games programme in 1962.

**Answer: 1962**

questions.q: ’Manimahesh fair’ is held in which of the following state?
questions.solution:
The Manimahesh fair is held in Himachal Pradesh, in the Chamba region.

**Answer: Himachal Pradesh**

questions.q: ’Jaago’ dance is related to which of the following state?
questions.solution:
Jaago is associated with Punjab and celebratory wedding traditions.

**Answer: Punjab**

questions.q: Why can a geo-stationary satellite monitor the movement of clouds accurately?
options: Because it moves in North to South direction.
Because it moves in South to North direction.
Because it is stationary relative to any place on Earth.
Because it rotates faster than Earth.
questions.solution:
A geostationary satellite remains over the same point on Earth. This permits repeated monitoring of the same cloud region.

**Answer: Because it is stationary relative to any place on Earth.**

questions.q: An object weighs 18 N when measured on the surface of the earth. What would be its weight when measured on the surface of the moon?
questions.solution:
Lunar gravity is approximately one-sixth of Earth’s. The weight is 18/6 = 3 N.

**Answer: 3 N**

questions.q: What immediate measure was taken in 1991 to resolve the balance of payments crisis in India?
options: Devaluation of the rupee against foreign currencies.
Revaluation of the rupee against foreign currencies.
questions.solution:
India devalued the rupee in July 1991 as part of its response to the balance-of-payments crisis.

**Answer: Devaluation of the rupee against foreign currencies.**

questions.q: In which year did Maharaja Ranjit Singh established his capital at Lahore?
questions.solution:
Ranjit Singh captured Lahore and established it as his capital in 1799.

**Answer: 1799**

questions.q: As per the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act-2003, which of the following is NOT laid before both the house of parliament along with Annual Financial statement?
options: The medium term fiscal policy statement
questions.solution:
The monetary policy statement is not one of the three fiscal statements specified here. Monetary policy is a central-bank function.

**Answer: The monetary policy statement**

questions.q:
Which of the following organ can be donated while the donor is alive?

I. Part of a liver

II. Kidney
questions.solution:
A living donor can donate one kidney or part of the liver, subject to medical evaluation. Both statements are correct.

**Answer: Both I and II**

questions.q: The most important achievement of Shishunaga was ____.
options: defeating Avanti (Malwa) and annexing it to Magadh
questions.solution:
Shishunaga defeated Avanti and incorporated it into Magadha, ending the long rivalry between the kingdoms.

**Answer: defeating Avanti (Malwa) and annexing it to Magadh**
